title: Restoration lifecycle
intro: A transparent, repeatable process you can apply to any facility or restoration project. Each phase has roles people can take on based on their gifts, time, and resources. Two connected loops describe on-site restoration work and the planning pipeline that funds, designs, and obtains what you need before that work happens.

phases.title: Stewardship funding
phases.summary: Seed and sustain a dedicated maintenance fund.
bullets: Contribute financial support to the maintenance pool.
Enable predictable repair and replacement work instead of emergency-only fixes.
Support a transparent ledger that is publicly viewable in an anonymous format.

phases.title: Issue spotting and reporting
phases.summary: Identify maintenance needs and submit clear field reports.
bullets: Take a maintenance tag from a QR station.
Wrap or attach the tag to the broken item or area that needs attention.
Scan the tag's code with a phone.
Capture a photo and submit a short issue report.
Send the report into a review queue for approval and prioritization.

phases.title: Repair and fabrication
phases.summary: Provide the craftsmanship and technical labor needed to complete approved work.
bullets: Evaluate approved requests and define the repair plan.
Repair, replace, fabricate, or otherwise maintain the affected item.
Document work completion so the maintenance history remains traceable.
Return the maintenance tag to the QR station so it can be reused for future issues.

phases.title: Accountability and continuity
bullets: Funding activity remains transparent and trusted.
Completed work is logged for future reference.
New issues cycle back into the spotting phase.
The organization keeps a living, maintainable maintenance schedule.

restorationLoop.title: Restoration lifecycle
restorationLoop.centerNote: On site: spot what needs care, prepare the work, then restore in place.

phaseDetails.label: Spot
phaseDetails.description: See what is wrong, mark it in the building, and get a clear report into the system so the parish can prioritize it.

subItems.title: Identify
subItems.description: See what needs attention and pick up a tag from a QR station so every issue is tied to a known place and workflow.

subItems.title: Tag
subItems.description: Wrap or attach the tag on the broken item or area so others can see that it is logged.

subItems.title: Report
subItems.description: Scan the code with a phone and submit photos and notes through the website or app (app to come)—same idea as a work request, but built for church maintenance.

phaseDetails.label: Prepare
phaseDetails.description: Line up people, time, hospitality, and attention so volunteers and crews can show up ready—not only tools and materials, but the human side of a work day.

subItems.title: Schedules
subItems.description: Coordinate dates, shifts, and who is on site so nothing depends on a last-minute scramble.

subItems.title: Meals and beverages
subItems.description: When it fits the day, organize food and drinks for volunteers and crews.

subItems.title: Sign-ups and events
subItems.description: Let people register for restoration work days and know what to expect.

subItems.title: Promotion and campaigns
subItems.description: Share the need on social media, bulletins, and other channels so the parish knows how to help.

phaseDetails.label: Restore
phaseDetails.description: Do the agreed work on the building and close the loop so what was promised actually gets finished.

subItems.title: Hands-on work
subItems.description: Repair, fabricate, install, and touch the real materials—this is where craft meets the building.

subItems.title: Complete the work items
subItems.description: Finish the tasks that were scoped and checked off so nothing is left half-done without a reason.

subItems.title: Documentation
subItems.description: Record what was done for history, safety, and the next person who cares for the space.

planningLoop.title: Planning lifecycle
planningLoop.centerNote: Fund the effort, research and design, then make and procure what restoration will need—parts, materials, fabricated pieces—before and alongside the work on site.

phaseDetails.label: Fund
phaseDetails.description: Secure money and transparency so projects are possible and donors can trust how resources are used.

subItems.title: Stewardship and gifts
subItems.description: Channel donations and dedicated maintenance funds toward predictable repair instead of only emergencies.

subItems.title: Transparent ledger
subItems.description: Keep a view of spending that the community can trust, in a form that respects privacy where needed.

phaseDetails.label: R&D
phaseDetails.description: Figure out what to build, how it should fit, and what can be printed, fabricated, or ordered.

subItems.title: Research and design
subItems.description: Turn field reports into plans, drawings, and specs that volunteers and vendors can follow.

subItems.title: Try and refine
subItems.description: Prototype ideas—3D prints, mock-ups, test fits—before committing to full production.

phaseDetails.label: Make & procure
phaseDetails.description: Bring physical things to the job: make them in-house or buy them, often both in the same initiative.

subItems.title: Manufacture
subItems.description: Print, cut, or build parts—3D printing, woodwork, metalwork, whatever matches the plan.

subItems.title: Procure
subItems.description: Order hardware, stock, and items you will not make yourself so they arrive when the crew needs them.

subItems.title: Staging
subItems.description: Line up delivery and storage so materials are ready when the restoration day arrives.
